app.title: Who Really Sent This?
app.tagline: Paste an email's headers. Find out who really sent it.
app.paste_help: The full message is fine too. We only read the headers.
app.empty_paste: Please paste the email headers first.
app.privacy: Nothing you paste is saved or sent anywhere. It is checked here and then thrown away.

guide.title: How do I find the headers?
guide.intro: Every email has hidden lines called headers. They show where it really came from. Here is how to copy them.
guide.gmail: **Gmail:** open the email. Click the three dots (⋮) next to Reply. Choose **Show original**. Click **Copy to clipboard**.
guide.outlook: **Outlook.com:** open the email. Click the three dots (…). Choose **View**, then **View message source**. Select all and copy.
guide.outlook_desktop: **Outlook on a computer:** open the email. Choose **File**, then **Properties**. Copy the box called **Internet headers**.
guide.yahoo: **Yahoo Mail:** open the email. Click the three dots (…). Choose **View raw message**. Select all and copy.
guide.apple: **Apple Mail (Mac):** open the email. Choose **View**, then **Message**, then **Raw Source**. Select all and copy.

CHECKS_OUT.title: Checks out
CHECKS_OUT.sentence: This email really came from the address it shows.

BE_CAREFUL.title: Be careful
BE_CAREFUL.sentence: Something about this email is not right. Check it another way before you act.

LIKELY_SCAM.title: Likely a scam
LIKELY_SCAM.sentence: This email is not from who it says. Do not click, reply, or pay.

rule.RULE_DMARC_FAIL_ENFORCED: The real owner of this address asked mail services to block fakes. This email failed that test.
rule.RULE_UNAUTHENTICATED_IMPERSONATION: It uses the name of a known company or office. Nothing proves it came from them.
rule.RULE_LOOKALIKE_INSTITUTION_DOMAIN: The address looks like a real company's address, but it is a copy.
rule.RULE_INSTITUTION_NAME_WRONG_DOMAIN: The name says it is {name}. The address is not theirs.
rule.RULE_ADDRESS_DISGUISED_AS_NAME: The name shown is an email address. The real sender is a different one.
rule.RULE_INVALID_FROM_DOMAIN: The sender's address ends in a way that does not exist on the internet.
rule.RULE_FORGED_PROVIDER_HOP: The email contains a fake line that pretends your mail service handled it.
rule.RULE_INCOMPLETE_HEADERS: Some of the headers are missing. Copy them again, all of them, and check again.
rule.RULE_NO_DMARC: The sender's address has no clear proof that it is real.
rule.RULE_NOT_ALIGNED: The address you see is not the one that was checked.
rule.RULE_REPLY_TO_ELSEWHERE: If you reply, your answer goes to someone else.
rule.RULE_FREEMAIL_INSTITUTION: It uses the name of {name}, but it comes from a free email account. Real offices do not do that.
rule.RULE_UNRELATED_FIRST_SERVER: It started at a computer that has nothing to do with the sender.
rule.RULE_ODD_ROUTE: The times on this email's route do not make sense.

note.NOTE_PASS_NOT_SAFE: This only shows who sent it. A real sender can still send a bad link. If it asks for money or passwords, check with them another way.

who.title: Who it says it is from, and where it came from
who.vouched: Domain that proved it sent this
who.first_server: First outside computer your mail service saw
who.claims: This email says it is from **{name}**. Their real address ends in **{domains}**.
who.lookalike: **{shown}** is made to look like **{real}**. It is not the same website.
who.punycode: The address uses hidden foreign letters. It shows up as **{decoded}**.

auth.title: The three checks, in plain words
auth.spf_what: Was the computer that sent this allowed to send for {domain}?
auth.dkim_what: Does the email carry a digital signature, and is it unbroken?
auth.dmarc_what: Did it pass the test that the owner of {domain} set for real email?
auth.policy_quarantine: The owner says: send fakes to spam.
auth.policy_none: The owner only watches. Fakes are not blocked.
auth.aligned_yes: The address you see matches a domain that passed a check.
auth.aligned_no: The address you see does not match any domain that passed a check.
auth.your_provider: These results were written by {provider} when the email arrived.

flags.title: Red flags
flags.ID_REPLY_TO_MISMATCH: Replies go to a different address: {reply_to}.
flags.ID_RETURN_PATH_MISMATCH: Bounced mail goes to a different domain. Mail services do this often, so on its own it is not a problem.
flags.ID_FREEMAIL_FROM: It was sent from a free email account.
flags.ID_FROM_DOMAIN_INVALID: The sender's address ends in a way that does not exist.
flags.LOOK_DISPLAY_NAME_SPOOF: The name does not match the address.
flags.LOOK_LOOKALIKE_DOMAIN: The address is a lookalike of a real one.
flags.LOOK_PUNYCODE_DOMAIN: The address hides foreign letters that look like normal ones.
flags.LOOK_FREEMAIL_INSTITUTION: A company or office name, sent from a free email account.
flags.LOOK_ADDRESS_IN_NAME: The name shown is a different email address.
flags.HOP_FORGED_PROVIDER: A line in the route was faked by the sender.
flags.HOP_ENTRY_UNRELATED: The first computer has nothing to do with the sender.
flags.HOP_TIME_REVERSED: The route goes backwards in time.
flags.HOP_LONG_DELAY: The email waited more than a day somewhere on its way.
flags.HOP_MALFORMED: Some route lines are hard to read.
flags.NORM_NO_HEADERS_FOUND: No email headers were found in what you pasted.
flags.NORM_MISSING_AUTH_RESULTS: The check results from your mail service are missing.
flags.NORM_INPUT_TOO_LARGE: The paste is very long. Only the first part was checked.
flags.TRUST_NO_STAMP: Your mail service's check results were not found.
flags.TRUST_GENERIC_STAMP: We did not recognize your mail service, so these results are less certain.

journey.title: The journey
journey.intro: Each step is one computer that passed the email along, from the first one to your inbox.
journey.claimed: Claimed by the sender (could be made up)
journey.entry: Your mail service received it here

why.title: Why this answer
why.none: Everything we can check passed, and nothing looked wrong.

todo.title: What to do next
todo.dont_click: Do not click links or call phone numbers in the email.
todo.go_direct: Go to the real website yourself. Type the address. Do not use the email's links.
todo.never_share: Never send passwords, codes, or bank details by email.
todo.ask: Not sure? Call the company using a number you already trust, like the one on your card or bill.
todo.report_in_app: Report it in your email app: in Gmail, use the three dots and choose **Report phishing**. In Outlook, choose **Report** and then **Report phishing**.
todo.report_ftc: Report scams to the Federal Trade Commission
todo.report_ic3: Report online crime to the FBI
todo.report_bank: For a bank, call the number on the back of your card.
todo.report_school: For a school, call the school office directly.

limits.title: What this tool cannot tell you
limits.text: A pass means the owner of the address sent the email. It does not mean the email is safe. A real account that was hacked will pass. So will a scam sent from an ordinary Gmail account. This tool reads only what you paste. It does not open links or look anything up.
